## The Dog That Befriended the Burglar

If there is one story dominating the social sphere this week, it is undoubtedly the tale of Nash, a four-year-old Golden Retriever from San Diego. While owners Dante Rowley and Stephanie Calderon were away enduring a local heatwave, an intruder forced his way through a window. Instead of barking, biting, or fleeing, Nash did what Golden Retrievers do best: he brought the burglar a tennis ball to play with.

The viral video captures the thief standing awkwardly while Nash wagged his tail, effectively ignoring the break-in in favor of a game. The owners, amused by the footage, jokingly declared Nash "the worst guard dog in history." The post highlights the breed’s characteristic friendliness and desire to retrieve, turning a potential home invasion into a wholesome interaction. Social media reactions have been overwhelmingly positive, with many users noting that Nash’s love for toys outweighs his protective instincts. It’s a charming reminder that sometimes the best security system is just a good boy.

## AI Watermarking: Not So Passive After All

In the world of technology, a counterintuitive finding from *Ars Technica* has sparked debate regarding AI text watermarking. The report reveals that watermarking is not merely passive metadata tagging but an active mechanism that influences the token sampler and alters subsequent model computations. This means that language models with watermarking enabled are actually more vulnerable to adversarial prompts—a significant shift in understanding how these systems function.

The discussion, primarily hosted on Bluesky, reflects a growing impatience within the tech community. User @Doll mocked the slow pace of engineering insights, noting that it took extensive benchmarks and charts to validate what seemed obvious: "fucking with token selection" has measurable effects on model security. The consensus suggests a frustration with academic or corporate delays in recognizing practical technical realities. For developers, this implies that as watermarking becomes standard to detect AI-generated content, it may inadvertently open new attack vectors for those looking to manipulate or bypass AI filters.

## Control Resonant Launches to Global Fans

Gaming enthusiasts are preparing for the release of *Control Resonant*, the latest title from Remedy Entertainment, set to launch on September 24th. Community engagement is already high, particularly regarding developer @Chip, who contributed to the game’s trailers and announced he will be streaming the release on Twitch.

The post serves as a logistical hub for players, providing precise launch times across multiple global time zones, including 10 AM EDT and 3 PM BST. This focus on cross-platform accessibility and direct developer involvement highlights Remedy’s strategy to connect directly with its fanbase during the debut. For those waiting to dive into the Resonant universe, the clock is ticking.

## Quick Hits

*   **India-New Zealand Trade:** The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) has been officially ratified and is scheduled to enter into force on October 20. This diplomatic milestone, highlighted by *The Hindu*, signals deeper economic ties, with current discussion focused on the timeline of implementation rather than conflicting opinions.
*   **FAW Community Update:** A user from r/ForeverAloneDating shared the struggle of being a 24-year-old woman who has never been kissed or dated. While she has accepted her status, she seeks a compromise to alleviate the silent judgment and disappointment from her parents, who continue to compare her to her mother’s early marriage at age 23.
*   **Anime Music Nostalgia:** Fans of *Cardcaptor Sakura* are revisiting the 1998 ending theme "Groovy" by Koumi Hirose. Produced by Studio Madhouse, the track remains a key element of the show's soundtrack, with the post serving as a nostalgic nod for collectors of anime music.
*   **Audio Innovation:** @Audio Plugin Guy (Stu) announced the release of True Panner, a free stereo panning plugin for macOS and Windows. Developed by The Note Audio, it combines standard balance controls with Interaural Time Difference (ITD) panning to create more natural stereo placement and improved spatial imaging.
*   **Dog Photography Humor:** In a lighthearted observation from Bluesky, user @bakoon highlighted the visual illusion created in dog jumping competitions. Freezing the frame at the peak of a jump makes the canine appear to be riding an invisible bicycle, a whimsical analogy that resonates with internet users finding humor in athletic postures.
*   **4chan Bird Spotting:** The "/rpt/ Recent Photo Thread" on 4chan featured an "Unsuccessful Tries" edition focused on identifying birds in ambiguous images. Users engaged in meme-style dialogue, with one caption reading "i see bird i feel better," reflecting the casual satisfaction of solving minor visual puzzles.
*   **Graffiti Culture Spotlight:** A cryptic but celebratory post on Bluesky by @Soup Of Graffiti titled "Knight of the Cool S" spotlights a specific entity within street art culture. Likely referencing a respected artist or piece associated with the "Cool S" graffiti alphabet, the post serves as an honorary designation for those familiar with the niche.

@Italian News by RSS (ItalianNews@mastodon.ozioso.online) — Il Fatto Quotidiano: “È il peggior cane da guardia”: un ladro entra in casa mentre i proprietari sono via, il golden retriever lo accoglie portandogli la palla per giocare “Nash è il peggiore cane da guardia” hanno sentenziato Dante Rowley e Stephanie Calderon a proposito del loro golden retriever. A spingere loro a pronunciare queste parole nei confronti del proprio cane è stato quanto è successo lo scorso 5 settembre, mentre si trovavano fuori dalla loro abitazione a San Diego, in California. La coppia, durante una delle ondate di calore più intense dell’anno, era lontana dalla città quando ha ricevuto un avviso con il quale si segnalava l’intrusione nella propria abitazione da parte di un estraneo. All’interno della casa, però, c’era il loro golden retriever di quattro anni, Nash. Quando il cane si è accorto della presenza dell’uomo, ha cercato di farlo giocare con sé. “È super amichevole e giocherellone” ha spiegato Rowley. Come si può vedere nelle immagini che la coppia ha condiviso sui propri social, il cane si avvicina all’uomo tenendo una palla in bocca. Uno dei suoi giochi preferiti, infatti, come spiegato dal suo proprietario, è quello di riportare la pallina da tennis che gli viene lanciata. “Adora giocare a riportare palline da tennis o peluche” ha raccontato sempre Rowley. L’uomo che si era introdotto nell’abitazione forzando una finestra non ha però assecondato il desiderio del cane. Pochi istanti dopo è stato un altro evento a sorprendere Nash. L'articolo “È il peggior cane da guardia”: un ladro entra in casa mentre i proprietari sono via, il golden retriever lo accoglie portandogli la palla per giocare proviene da Il Fatto Quotidiano. “It’s the worst guard dog”: a thief enters the house while the owners are away, the golden retriever greets him by bringing him the ball to play with. “Nash is the worst guard dog,” declared Dante Rowley and Stephanie Calderon regarding their golden retriever. What pushed them to utter these words about their canine was what happened on September 5th, while they were outside their home in San Diego, California. The couple, during one of the most intense heat waves of the year, were away from the city when they received an alert reporting a break-in at their residence by a stranger. Inside the house, however, was their four-year-old golden retriever, Nash. When the dog realized the presence of the man, he tried to play with him. “He’s super friendly and playful,” Rowley explained. As you can see in the images that the couple shared on their social media, the dog approaches the man while holding a ball in his mouth. One of his favorite games, as explained by his owner, is retrieving tennis balls that are thrown to him. “He loves playing with tennis balls or plush toys,” Rowley always said. The man who had broken into the residence by forcing a window did not, however, accommodate the dog’s desire. Shortly after, another event surprised Nash. clusters.summary: Dante Rowley and Stephanie Calderon of San Diego, California, shared viral images of their four-year-old Golden Retriever, Nash, welcoming a burglar into their home on September 5. Instead of barking or attacking, the dog greeted the intruder—who had entered by forcing a window—by bringing him a tennis ball to play with. The owners, observing the incident during a heat wave while away from the city, humorously declared Nash "the worst guard dog" due to his super friendly and playful nature. Although the thief did not engage in play, the video highlights the breed's characteristic friendliness over protective instinct. Social media reactions emphasize Nash's lack of aggression, with many noting his love for retrieving toys as the reason he ignored the break-in.
